Typical Human Cell • Cell theory • A cell is the structural and functional unit of life. All living organisms are composed of cells • Human is multicellular organism • Human body is composed of many cells • Over 200 different types of human cells • Types differ in size, shape, and subcellular components; these differences lead to differences in functions

Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Mitochondrion (Mitochondria) • “power plant” of cell • Perform aerobic (oxygen-requiring) cellular respiration to produce most of cell’s energy • Formed by 2 membranes Which type of cell, fat cell or muscle cell, has more mitochondria in cytoplasm? Why?

Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Rough ER • External surface appears rough because of the attached ribosomes • Site of synthesis of proteins and phospholipids • Final protein is enclosed in vesicle and sent to Golgi body for further processing • Smooth ER • Cholesterol and steroid-based hormone synthesis • Converting of glycogen to free glucose • Storage and release of calcium ions

Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Rough ER • External surface appears rough because of the attached ribosomes • Site of synthesis of proteins and phospholipids • Final protein is enclosed in vesicle and sent to Golgi body for further processing • Smooth ER • Cholesterol and steroid-based hormone synthesis • Converting of glycogen to free glucose • Storage and release of calcium ions

Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Nucleus • Largest organelle • Contains the genetic information (Chromosomes) for synthesis of nearly all proteins • Responds to signals to control the kinds and amounts of proteins to be produced • Most cells are uninucleate (one nucleus) • Skeletal muscle cells, some bone cells, and some liver cells are multinucleate (many nuclei) • Mature red blood cells are anucleate (no nucleus)
